title: Earth fact of the day, #2 - Marginal REVOLUTION
gist: Cowen quotes a Washington Post analysis of IEA data showing prolonged oil and gas shortages are driving the largest annual decline in fossil fuel consumption and carbon emissions since the pandemic, with crude demand at 102 million bpd in the latest IEA forecast versus 91 million in 2020.

insights.claim: Prolonged oil and gas shortages are driving down global fossil fuel consumption and carbon emissions, according to a Washington Post analysis of International Energy Agency data.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: Supply shortage is causing measurable demand destruction—a key signal for oil and gas price and volume outlooks.
insights.quote: The shortages have gone on for so long that they are aggressively driving down how much carbon is being released into the atmosphere

insights.claim: Such an annual decline in fossil fuel use has not happened since the height of the coronavirus pandemic.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: Places the current energy shock in a historical context of rare demand contractions.
insights.quote: Such an annual decline has not happened since the height of the coronavirus pandemic.

insights.claim: Crude oil demand averaged 91 million barrels per day in 2020 versus 102 million barrels per day under the latest IEA forecast.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: Demand remains well above pandemic levels despite the drop, bounding downside for oil volumes.
insights.quote: Crude oil demand averaged 91 million barrels per day in 2020, compared with 102 million barrels per day under the latest IEA forecast.

insights.claim: This year's drop is substantial especially given that a sharp increase in demand had initially been forecast.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: Large gap between forecast and realized demand signals forecast risk for energy models.

insights.claim: Cowen judges the shortage-induced emissions decline as not a good thing overall but suggests it carries a lesson.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: Implies price/scarcity, not policy, is the effective lever on emissions.
